title: I'm so lost in what to watch nowadays. I mean I've yet to watch 1/3 of all the quality films ppl normally list off. That's fine but I'm not much of a mainstream person. I considered them as acquired taste so I can watch underrated films as the norm. I'm just don't know where to find hidden gems.

commenti.body:
I understand. I take my film time seriously and many people think I'm crazy or difficult for wanting to watch films that makes me think or feel deeply (or both). For them films are just something they kill time with and don't have to think about.

You can look for lesser-known, arthouse type of films by first identifying your favourite genres. What kind of films do you like to watch?

Hey, i get what you mean. Recently ive just been looking on the Criterion Collection website and picking movies to watch from that. You cant go wrong, they are all classic!

[https://www.criterion.com/shop/browse?sort=spine\_number](https://www.criterion.com/shop/browse?sort=spine_number)

Hard to be a God 


Russian film, pretty sure it's available on YouTube etc


Don't do any research into it, just experience it.


Bella Tarr's films always impress me. I see something new in them every time

Thanks. I don't have a favorite genre. I watch them all. These days my family watches a lot of superhero fantasy films and series. Had to sit through The Boys which wasn't as good as people say it is. I finished watching Barry. It was not bad! It was just a tad refreshing. Haha Sorry I dont have favorite genre.

[https://cinemageddon.net/](https://cinemageddon.net/)  
[https://karagarga.in/](https://karagarga.in/)

Also, if your after niche repositories of film, try these. They can be challenging to become member of, but there is allot there.

[https://letterboxd.com/gubarenko/list/1001-movies-you-must-see-before-you-die-2021/](https://letterboxd.com/gubarenko/list/1001-movies-you-must-see-before-you-die-2021/)

Maybe this list could help you. There's definitely a lot of mainstream media here too, but you can just pass that and focus on what you are looking for. I'd suggest to just start from what inspires you the most. I've only watched 25% of this list so i use it a lot when i need to choose what to watch next.

Both fall into the slow cinema category, but Tarr is the champion of it


If you want 'Experiences', this is a great starting point.

You mentioned you've seen about 1/3 of the quality films people normally list. Which list you're looking at matters a lot in terms of what films pop up! IMDB is going to give a different list than Sight&Sound. In my opinion, the best composite list is TheyShootPictures:

[https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000\_rank1-1000.htm](https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_rank1-1000.htm)
Would pay to be a part of those 2 sites.

Unironically I've been using ChatGPT to insert my favourite films and generate suggestions for other films with similar commonalities. Also browsing letterboxd lists helps as the films are generally more thoughtful and arthouse-slanted than your general audience lists from IMDb and such.
